method: Old/new comparison with subagents that read the skill files from disk and could open references, as in normal use. Iteration 1 ran cases 1 to 5 once per version. Iteration 2 ran cases 1 and 6 twice per version after tightening the bold wording. Assertions were checked by a script (code spans matched per span, bold inside and outside checklists, Slack syntax, word counts) and drafts were reviewed inline. This tests drafting, not automatic skill loading.
findings: Both versions show identifiers as code when the prompt names them as hosts, buckets or projects.
The old skill left ports as plain text in a short comment in both runs; the new skill showed them as code in both runs.
The old skill never bolded the problem or wanted result in issue prose; the new skill did in every run.
With raw Slack mrkdwn, only the new skill started with a bold lead line. Both used single-asterisk bold and Slack link syntax.
The first new-skill wording bolded a whole sentence. Limiting bold to two to five words fixed it in iteration 2.
Parent issue, Markdown table and small-fix cases passed for both versions, with no extra formatting on the small fix.
